rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reply to the regress objection distinguishes contingent indwelling from the necessary fact of its being located; the latter need not itself require another indwelling.
rows.anchor: حلوله في المحل لما كان جائزا كان حلوله في المحل زائدا عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God’s essence suffices for indwelling, the result entails either an eternal substrate or a newly occurring attribute; if not, a new cause arises in God, also impossible.
rows.anchor: ذاته ، إما أن تكون كافية اقتضاء هذا الحلول أو لا تكون كافية في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God cannot receive temporal accidents: if receptive, He would have been receptive to them eternally; the analogy with His eternal power to create therefore fails.
rows.anchor: لو كانت ذاته قابلة / للحوادث لكانت في الأزل قابلة لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If divine knowledge entered Jesus, it either remained in God too, putting one attribute in two loci and implying the same for everyone, or left God and made Him no longer knowing.
rows.anchor: العلم لما حل في عيسى ففي تلك الحالة إما أن يقال إنه بقي في ذات الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a debate, al-Razi asks why a permitted union or indwelling would be confined to Jesus rather than Zayd, Amr, animals, or plants.
rows.anchor: إذا جوزت اتحاد كلمة الله تعالى بعيسى أو حلولها فيه فكيف عرفت أن كلمة الله تعالى ما دخلت في زيد وعمرو

rows.speaker: بعض النصارى
rows.claim: The Christian interlocutor says Jesus alone showed raising the dead and healing the blind and lepers, which proves union or indwelling in him.
rows.anchor: إنما أثبتنا ذلك الاتحاد أو الحلول بناء على ما ظهر على يد عيسى عليه السلام من إحياء الموتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi replies that the Christian had conceded absence of evidence does not prove absence, so lack of miracles elsewhere cannot prove that union is absent from other beings.
rows.anchor: عدم الدليل لا يدل على عدم المدلول فلا يلزم من عدم ظهور هذه الخوارق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A doctrine that permits union with every creature, including animals and plants, leads to an absurd conclusion and must be false.
rows.anchor: في حق كل واحد بل في حق كل حيوان ونبات ولا شك أن المذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raising the dead and healing do not prove divinity: Moses’ staff becoming a serpent was a greater transformation yet did not make Moses divine.
rows.anchor: انقلاب العصا ثعبانا أبعد من انقلاب الميت حيا فإذا ظهر ذلك على يد موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus’ worship and withdrawal from worldly life indicate servanthood more strongly than divinity; his reported weakness and being killed by Jews do not suit lordship.
rows.anchor: دلالة أحوال عيسى على العبودية أقوى من دلالتها على الربوبية لأنه كان مجتهدا في العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus must be either eternal or originated: his birth, childhood, growth, eating, and drinking show he was originated, and an originated being is created and a servant.
rows.anchor: بالضرورة أنه ولد وكان طفلا ثم صار شابا وكان يأكل ويشرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if a divine attribute indwelled in Jesus, the human locus remains originated and created, so Jesus is still an originated servant rather than God.
rows.anchor: الحال هو صفة الإله والمسيح هو المحل والمحل محدث مخلوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A child must share the parent’s kind: distinction adds composition to God, making the Necessary Being composite and therefore possible, an absurdity.
rows.anchor: فيلزم وقوع التركيب في ذات الله وكل مركب ممكن ، فالواجب ممكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposal that Jesus was God because God specially empowered him to create bodies fails against Christian reports that he was weak and killed.
rows.anchor: النصارى حكوا عنه الضعف والعجز وأن اليهود قتلوه ولو كان قادرا على خلق الأجسام

rows.speaker: الأرميوسية
rows.claim: A group called the Ariumiyya took sonship to mean adoption for honor; al-Razi says the error is largely verbal.
rows.anchor: اتخذه ابنا لنفسه على سبيل التشريف فهذا قد قال به قوم من النصارى يقال لهم الأرميوسية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These arguments establish the truth of God’s report that Jesus said, I am God’s servant.
rows.anchor: وبه ثبت صدق ما حكاه الله تعالى عنه

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most interpreters hold that Jesus uttered this speech in infancy; Abu al-Qasim al-Balkhi instead places it at an understanding adolescence before legal maturity.
rows.anchor: فالجمهور على أنه قال هذا الكلام حال صغره وقال أبو القاسم البلخي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One report from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, interprets Jesus as saying God had decreed that he would later be commissioned; he then fell silent and returned to infancy, becoming prophet at thirty.
rows.anchor: روى عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One position among those accepting infant speech is that Jesus was already a prophet as a child.
rows.anchor: أنه كان في ذلك الصغر نبيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Opponents argue that a prophet must be fully developed and that a baby’s challenge would repel listeners more than a woman’s.
rows.anchor: أن النبي لا يكون إلا كاملا والصغير ناقص الخلقة بحيث يعد هذا التحدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Opponents argue that full intellect must precede a prophetic claim, but miraculous intellect beforehand would put the miracle before the challenge.
rows.anchor: لو كان نبيا في هذا الصغر لكان كمال عقله مقدما على ادعائه للنبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Opponents argue that a child prophet should have taught laws; since no such teaching became famous or was transmitted, he was not yet a prophet.
rows.anchor: في ذلك الوقت لوجب أن يشتغل ببيان الأحكام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The defenders answer that God could remove the bodily smallness and limited understanding that might otherwise make the infant’s speech repellent.
rows.anchor: كون الصبي ناقصا ليس لذاته بل الأمر يرجع إلى صغر جسمه ونقصان فهمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They answer that prior miraculous intellect could be a sign for Zechariah, a precursor to Jesus’ prophethood, or a gift to Mary; al-Razi says these are permissible.
rows.anchor: إكمال عقله وإن حصل مقدما على دعواه إلا أنه معجزة لزكريا عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They answer that Jesus could initially be sent without detailing laws, then explain the laws after reaching maturity.
rows.anchor: مجرد بعثته إليهم من غير بيان شيء من الشرائع والأحكام جائز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi finds no impossibility in infant prophethood and prefers the verse’s apparent meaning over Ibn Abbas’s later-commission interpretation.
rows.anchor: يدل على كونه نبيا في ذلك الوقت فوجب إجراؤه على ظاهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Balkhi’s adolescent timing is remote because Jesus had to speak when suspicion fell on Mary.
rows.anchor: أما قول أبي القاسم البلخي فبعيد وذلك لأن الحاجة إلى كلام عيسى عليه السلام إنما كانت عند وقوع التهمة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the definite article in “the Book” points to the familiar Torah.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم هو التوراة لأن الألف واللام في الكتاب تنصرف للمعهود

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim says “the Book” means the Gospel, with the article marking the genus of scripture.
rows.anchor: المراد هو الإنجيل لأن الألف واللام ههنا للجنس أي آتاني

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Others say Jesus received both Torah and Gospel because the definite article conveys totality.
rows.anchor: المراد هو التوراة والإنجيل لأن الألف واللام تفيد الاستغراق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording indicates that the Book, prophethood, and commands to pray, give alms, and call people to God were granted before Jesus spoke, perhaps immediately before or much earlier.
rows.anchor: يدل على أن ذلك كان قد حصل من قبل إما ملاصقا لذلك الكلام أو متقدما عليه بأزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account places the revelation and prophethood while Jesus was in the womb; another says they came after birth, when he told his mother he would clear her name.
rows.anchor: فقيل هذا الوحي نزل عليه وهو في بطن أمه وقيل لما انفصل من الأم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say Jesus was a prophet but not a messenger yet because he had not brought a law, construing prophet as one of elevated rank.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم أخبر أنه نبي ولكنه ما كان رسولا لأنه في ذلك الوقت ما جاء بالشريعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi rejects that definition: in religious usage, especially alongside a law and commands, a prophet is one whom God grants prophethood and messengership.
rows.anchor: وهذا ضعيف لأن النبي في عرف الشرع هو الذي خصه الله بالنبوة وبالرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A proposed objection says Jesus could not be blessed when his coming coincided with some people becoming Jews or Christians and few remaining on truth.
rows.anchor: كيف جعله مباركا والناس كانوا قبله على الملة الصحيحة فلما جاء صار بعضهم يهودا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation derives blessing from steadfastness, from the image of a camel kneeling: Jesus was made steadfast in God’s religion.
rows.anchor: البركة في اللغة هي الثبات وأصله من بروك البعير فمعناه جعلني ثابتا على دين الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus was blessed by teaching people their religion and calling them to truth; people’s later error is their own, not his.
rows.anchor: إنما كان مباركا لأنه كان يعلم الناس دينهم ويدعوهم إلى طريق الحق فإن ضلوا فمن قبل أنفسهم

rows.speaker: الحسن عن النبي
rows.claim: A report says Mary sent Jesus to a teacher after asking him not to strike the child; Jesus explained the letters of Abjad as signs of God’s attributes and giving God His due.
rows.anchor: وروى الحسن عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : أسلمت أم عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes blessing as increase and elevation: Jesus would prevail by proof in earthly life and then be raised to heaven.
rows.anchor: فكأنه قال : جعلني في جميع الأحوال غالبا مفلحا منجحا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada reports that a woman blessed Mary’s womb and breast after seeing Jesus revive the dead and heal; Jesus replied that true felicity belongs to one who follows the Book without arrogance.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة أنه رأته امرأة وهو يحيي الموتى ويبرىء الأكمة والأبرص فقالت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “wherever I am” indicates that Jesus’ state did not change as though he returned to infancy and lost legal responsibility.
rows.anchor: فهو يدل على أن حاله لم يتغير كما قيل إنه عاد إلى حال الصغر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against the objection that a child is exempt from prayer and alms, one answer is that Jesus was commanded to perform them after reaching maturity.
rows.anchor: لا يدل على أنه تعالى أوصاه بأدائهما في الحال بل بعد البلوغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second answer says God made Jesus fully mature in body and intellect at birth, as He created Adam complete; al-Razi calls this closer to the apparent wording.
rows.anchor: لعل الله تعالى لما انفصل عيسى عن أمه صيره بالغا عاقلا تام الأعضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “As long as I live” suggests a lifelong obligation; because a fully formed adult speaking would not amaze the crowd, al-Razi proposes a small body with full strength and intellect.
rows.anchor: فإنه يفيد أن هذا التكليف متوجه عليه في جميع زمان حيائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus’ prayer and alms duty did not change while on earth, after his ascent, or at his later descent.
rows.anchor: والآية دالة على أن تكليفه لم يتغير حين كان في الأرض وحين رفع إلى السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s making Jesus dutiful to his mother supports the creation of human acts by God; taking it merely as divine assistance departs from the apparent sense.
rows.anchor: إن فعل العبد مخلوق لله تعالى لأن الآية تدل على أن كونه برا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus’ duty to honor Mary also implies her innocence of adultery, since an infallible messenger would not be commanded to honor an adulterous mother.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى تنزيه أمه عن الزنا إذ لو كانت زانية لما كان الرسول المعصوم مأمورا بتعظيمها

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf says Jesus’ very person was made dutiful because his filial piety was intense; the accusative is governed by an implied verb meaning “charged me.”
rows.anchor: جعل ذاته برا لفرط بره ونصبه بفعل في معنى أوصاني وهو كلفني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s making Jesus dutiful and not tyrannical marks a special distinction; if everyone were made this way, Jesus would have no particular merit.
rows.anchor: لما بين أنه جعله برا وما جعله جبارا فهذا إنما يحسن لو أن الله تعالى جعل غير جبارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Tyrannical” here means arrogant rather than humble toward his mother, and such arrogance would make him disobedient and wretched.
rows.anchor: أي ما جعلني متكبرا بل أنا خاضع لأني متواضع لها ولو كنت جبارا

rows.speaker: عيسى عليه السلام
rows.claim: Jesus is reported to have said that his heart was tender and he regarded himself as small.
rows.anchor: وروي أن عيسى عليه السلام قال : قلبي لين وأنا صغير في نفسي

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Some scholars say every disobedient person is tyrannical and wretched, citing this verse; they likewise cite 4:36 against a bad master.
rows.anchor: وعن بعض العلماء لا تجد العاق إلا جبارا شقيا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some take the article in “the peace” as referring to the peace previously given to John.
rows.anchor: لام التعريف في السلام منصرف إلى ما تقدم في قصتي يحيى

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf prefers the article as comprehensive: claiming all peace for Jesus and his followers leaves only a curse for Mary’s accusers, an insinuation suited to the hostile context.
rows.anchor: الصحيح أن يكون هذا التعريف تعويضا باللعن على من اتهم مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report has Jesus tell John that John is better because God gave him peace while Jesus gave peace to himself; al-Hasan answers that God’s greeting to Jesus is his own greeting.
rows.anchor: روى بعضهم عن عيسى عليه السلام أنه قال ليحيى أنت خير مني سلم الله عليك

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi explains peace as safety from harms and afflictions; Jesus asks for the safety granted to John at the three most vulnerable moments: birth, death, and resurrection.
rows.anchor: السلام عبارة عما يحصل به الأمان ومنه السلامة في النعم وزوال الآفات

rows.speaker: اليهود والنصارى
rows.claim: Jews and Christians deny that Jesus spoke in infancy, arguing that such a marvel would have spread widely and that Christians, devoted researchers, would know it.
rows.anchor: أن اليهود والنصارى ينكرون أن عيسى عليه السلام تكلم في زمان الطفولية

rows.speaker: اليهود والنصارى
rows.claim: They also argue that hostile Jews would have intensified their effort to kill Jesus had he claimed prophethood in infancy.
rows.anchor: ولأن اليهود أظهروا عداوته حال ما أظهر ادعاء النبوة

rows.speaker: المسلمون
rows.claim: Muslims argue that without Jesus’ speech clearing Mary, people would not have refrained from applying the adultery penalty; therefore he must have spoken in the cradle.
rows.anchor: أما المسلمون فقد احتجوا من جهة العقل على أنه تكلم فإنه لولا كلامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims answer that only a few people may have witnessed the speech, so it did not become famous, and the Jews may not have been present to hear it.
rows.anchor: بأنه ربما كان الحاضرون عند كلامه قليلين فلذلك لم يشتهر

rows.speaker: عاصم وابن عامر
rows.claim: Asim and Ibn Amir read “qawl al-haqq” in the accusative; Ibn Masud has “qāla al-haqq” or “qāla Allāh,” while al-Hasan reads it nominative, including at 6:73.
rows.anchor: قرأ عاصم وابن عامر : { قول الحق } بالنصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative can be a second predicate or predicate of an omitted subject; the accusative can be praise or an emphatic verbal noun.
rows.anchor: أما ارتفاعه فعلى أنه خبر بعد خبر أو خبر مبتدأ محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That Jesus, son of Mary” points back to the preceding description that he is God’s servant; the wording identifies Mary as his mother, not God as his father.
rows.anchor: أي ذلك الموصوف بهذه الصفات هو عيسى ابن مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading makes Jesus himself the “Word of Truth,” since al-Haqq is a name of God and “Word of God” and “Word of Truth” are equivalent.
rows.anchor: نفس عيسى عليه السلام هو قول الحق وذلك لأن الحق هو اسم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading supplies “the true saying”: the noun is attributed to its quality, emphasizing that Jesus is Mary’s son.
rows.anchor: إلا أنك أضفت الموصوف إلى الصفة فهو كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reading supplies an omitted subject: the description just given is the true, unalterable account, unlike their doubts.
rows.anchor: كأنه قيل ذلك عيسى ابن مريم ووصفنا له هو قول الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report about four learned leaders says one group called Jesus, God, and his mother gods, while the fourth said Jesus was God’s servant and messenger because he ate and slept.
rows.anchor: روي أن عيسى عليه السلام لما رفع حضر أربعة من أكابرهم وعلمائهم فقيل للأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “It is not for God to take a child” can mean that sonship is impossible or unfitting to divine wisdom and perfection, like saying God does not wrong.
rows.anchor: أن ثبوت الولد له محال

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba’i uses the verse to argue that God cannot do every conceivable act, since the text denies Him the choice to take a child.
rows.anchor: واحتج الجبائي بالآية بناء على هذا التفسير أنه ليس لله أن يفعل كل شيء

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Al-Razi’s Ash‘ari colleagues answer that lying is impossible for God, so the wording does not establish a general limit on divine power.
rows.anchor: وأجاب أصحابنا عنه بأنه الكذب محال على الله تعالى فلا جرم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “Be, and it is” passage proves God cannot have a child: an eternal child would either be another necessary being or a dependent servant, while an originated child is created and likewise a servant.
rows.anchor: فيكون عبدا له لا ولدا له فثبت أنه يستحيل أن يكون لله ولد

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: The Ash‘aris infer eternal divine speech because if “Be” were originated, its origin would require another command, causing an infinite regress.
rows.anchor: احتج الأصحاب بقوله : { إذا قضى أمرا فإنما يقول له كن فيكون }

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu‘tazila infer originated speech from the future marker “when,” the sequencing fāʾs, and the immediate succession of creation after the utterance.
rows.anchor: واحتج المعتزلة بالآية على حدوث كلام الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi says both proofs miss their target: the Ash‘ari proof makes the particular word “Be” eternal, while the Mu‘tazili proof concerns articulated letters and sounds, whose createdness is not disputed.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن استدلال الفريقين ضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking “Be” as a literal address fails: spoken before creation it addresses what does not exist, and spoken during creation it adds nothing to what power and will already produce.
rows.anchor: خطابا مع المعدوم وهو عبث وإن كان الثاني فهو حال حدوثه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view understands “Be” as creation or bringing into being: divine capacity is eternal, while actual creating is distinct and does not occur eternally.
rows.anchor: هو الخليق والتكوين وذلك لأن القدرة على الشيء غير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the takwin view, creation is distinct from the created thing; otherwise saying God created it by creating would mean that it produced itself.
rows.anchor: والتكوين ليس هو نفس المكون لأنا نقول المكون إنما حدث لأن الله تعالى كونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view treats “Be” metaphorically as God’s power and will taking effect among possible things without resistance, like a compliant servant.
rows.anchor: عبارة عن نفاذ قدرة الله تعالى ومشيئته في الممكنات

rows.speaker: المدنيون وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: The Medinese readers and Abu Amr open the hamza in “wa-inna,” yielding the sense “because God is my Lord and yours, worship Him.”
rows.anchor: قرأ المدنيون وأبو عمرو بفتح أن

rows.speaker: الكوفيون وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: The Kufans and Abu Ubayda read the hamza with kasra as a new clause; Ubayy’s codex has kasra without the conjunction, “because of this, worship Him.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون وأبو عبيدة بالكسر على الابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God would not say “God is my Lord,” the speech must be attributed either to Muhammad, commanded to announce Jesus’ servanthood, or to Jesus continuing his own statement.
rows.anchor: فلا بد وأن يكون قائل هذا غير الله تعالى

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم الأصفهاني
rows.claim: Abu Muslim treats the conjunction as continuing Jesus’ words: he is God’s servant, and God is his and the people’s Lord.
rows.anchor: قال أبو مسلم الأصفهاني : الواو في وإن الله

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb says Jesus entrusted them with the message that God is the Lord of all of them, since all are His servants.
rows.anchor: وقال وهب بن منبه عهد إليهم حين أخبرهم عن بعثه ومولده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God Lord refutes astrologers by locating human welfare and misery in God’s governance, and supports monotheism because no other Lord governs creation.
rows.anchor: يدل على أن مدبر الناس ومصلح أمورهم هو الله تعالى على خلاف قول المنجمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to worship follows the fitting description of God as Lord, showing worship is due because He grants every foundational and derivative blessing.
rows.anchor: ترتيب الحكم على الوصف المناسب مشعر بالعلية فههنا الأمر بالعبادة وقع مرتبا على ذكر وصف الربوبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s question about idols that cannot hear, see, or benefit shows by contrast that worship is owed to a benefactor; the connection holds in both directions.
rows.anchor: وبهذه الآية ثبت أن الله تعالى لما كان ربا ومربيا لعباده وجب عبادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is the creed of unity and denial of God’s child or consort; it is likened to a road because it leads to Paradise.
rows.anchor: يعني القول بالتوحيد ونفي الولد والصاحبة صراط مستقيم وأنه سمي هذا القول بالصراط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The factions” may mean Christian sects, Jews and Christians together, or all disbelievers including those contemporary with Muhammad; the last is clearer if the preceding speech addresses Muhammad.
rows.anchor: المراد فرق النصارى على ما بينا أقسامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The broad reading of all disbelievers is reinforced by the general warning to those who disbelieved.
rows.anchor: أي قل يا محمد إن الله ربي وربكم ، فهذا القول أظهر لأنه لا تخصيص فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The scene of a great day” can mean witnessing the terror of judgment, or its place or time; “testimony” can mean angels, prophets, or their own limbs testifying against them.
rows.anchor: فالمشهد إما أن يكون هو الشهود وما يتعلق به أو الشهادة وما يتعلق بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes the great scene the testimony people gave about Jesus and his mother.
rows.anchor: هو ما قالوه وشهدوا به في عيسى وأمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day is called great because its reckoning, questioning, reward, and punishment are unmatched.
rows.anchor: لأنه لا شيء أعظم مما يشاهد في ذلك اليوم من محاسبة ومساءلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wonder ordinarily means perceiving greatness while ignorant of its cause, but the word may express sheer astonishment even when its cause is known.
rows.anchor: التعجب هو استعظام الشيء مع الجهل بسبب عظمه

rows.speaker: سفيان عن شريح
rows.claim: Sufyan reports that Shurayh rejected attributing wonder to God, saying only the ignorant wonder.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء قال سفيان : قرأت عند شريح

rows.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
rows.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakha‘i answers that Shurayh was a poet impressed by his own learning, while Abdullah knew better: God’s action would cause wonder if done by people, as with divine scheming and mockery.
rows.anchor: فذكرت ذلك لإبراهيم النخعي فقال : إن شريحا شاعر يعجبه علمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians give several analyses of the exclamatory form: one derives it from “became generous,” cast as a command but meaning a statement.
rows.anchor: أكرم بزيد أصله أكرم زيد أي صار ذا كرم كأغد البعير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second analysis makes it an instruction to everyone to describe Zayd as generous, with an extra bāʾ, as in the wording about not throwing oneself into ruin.
rows.anchor: أن يقال إنه أمر لكل أحد بأن يجعل زيدا كريما أي بأن يصفه بالكرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third analysis says Zayd is so generous that he seems to embody generosity and help others attain their aim, like a pen that brings one to the intended writing.
rows.anchor: قولك أكرم بزيد يفيد أن زيدا بلغ في الكرم إلى حيث كأنه في ذاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The strongest, best-known reading is “How much they will hear and see!”; their faculties will astonish after their worldly deafness and blindness.
rows.anchor: وهو المشهور الأقوى أن معناه ما أسمعهم وما أبصرهم والتعجب على الله تعالى محال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading makes the words a threat about the painful things people will hear and see.
rows.anchor: التهديد مما سيسمعون وسيبصرون مما يسوء بصرهم

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi reads the words as a command to inform these people about those who come to God so that they take warning.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي ويحتمل أن يكون المراد أسمع هؤلاء وأبصرهم

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba’i reads them as making people hear and see these wrongdoers’ fate so they desist from similar conduct.
rows.anchor: الجبائي : ويجوز أسمع الناس بهؤلاء وأبصرهم بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers may be misguided now but recognize the truth in the afterlife, or remain astray from Paradise there, unlike believers.
rows.anchor: لكن الظالمون اليوم في ضلال مبين وفي الآخرة يعرفون الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning is addressed to Muhammad and his contemporaries, supporting the view that the factions who differed included people in his time; warning means frightening them with punishment.
rows.anchor: فلا شبهة في أنه أمر لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم بأن ينذر من في زمانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Regret is the Resurrection, when Hell’s people grieve; al-Razi rejects the view that even Paradise’s people regret missing higher ranks because grief is unfitting for the blessed.
rows.anchor: وقيل يتحسر أيضا في الجنة إذا لم يكن من السابقين الواصلين إلى الدرجات العالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “When the affair is decided” may mean the proofs about reward and punishment were completed; this is closer because the text says people remain heedless and unbelieving.
rows.anchor: إذ قضى الأمر ببيان الدلائل وشرح أمرالثواب والعقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reading places the decision at the end of the world on the Day of Regret, when worldly life and legal duty end.
rows.anchor: إذ قضى الأمر يوم الحسرة بفناء الدنيا وزوال التكليف

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet explained that death will be brought as a speckled ram and slaughtered before both groups, increasing Paradise’s joy and Hell’s grief.
rows.anchor: روي أنه سئل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since death is an accident, it cannot become an animal; the report means that there will be no death afterward.
rows.anchor: فلا يجوز أن يصير / جسما حيوانيا بل المراد أنه لا موت البتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People are heedless of that Day and the nature of its regret, and do not believe in the Day itself.
rows.anchor: أي عن ذلك اليوم وعن كيفية حسرته وهم لا يؤمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s inheriting the earth and its inhabitants means all benefit and harm ultimately belong to Him alone.
rows.anchor: أي هذه الأمور تؤول إلى أن لا يملك الضر والنفع إلا الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Returning to God means returning to His judgment and decree, not to a place, since God is beyond location; this is a grave warning to sinners.
rows.anchor: أي إلى محل حكمنا وقضائنا لأنه تعالى منزه عن المكان حتى يكون الرجوع إليه

none: Bare heading and verse text only.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura addresses monotheism, prophethood, and resurrection; its deniers include Christians who worship living intelligent beings and idolaters who worship inanimate things, with the latter’s error worse.
rows.anchor: الغرض من هذه السورة بيان التوحيد والنبوة والحشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction in “remember Abraham” links it to the earlier command to remember Zechariah, moving from his story to Abraham’s.
rows.anchor: والواو في قوله واذكر عطف على قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad and his people were not occupied with scholarship or books; his accurate account of this story without additions is therefore a compelling sign of prophethood.
rows.anchor: ما كان هو ولا قومه ولا أهل بلدته مشتغلين بالعلم ومطالعة الكتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham was the Arabs’ ancestor and they acknowledged his rank and pure faith; they should follow him, whether by ancestral authority or by examining his arguments.
rows.anchor: بعلو شأنه وطهارة دينه على ما قال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because many disbelievers defend ancestral religion, Abraham’s rejection of his own father’s faith and preference for proof rebuts them through their most honored forefather.
rows.anchor: كثيرا من الكفار في زمن الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم كانوا يقولون كيف نترك دين آبائنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story also answers those who cling to inherited worship and reject argument, as people who said they found their ancestors worshipping idols.
rows.anchor: أن كثيرا من الكفار كانوا يتمسكون بالتقليد وينكرون الاستدلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an shows Abraham reasoning rather than blindly imitating, instructing the audience that ancestral custom is an invalid proof.
rows.anchor: فحكى الله تعالى عن إبراهيم عليه السلام التمسك بطريقة الاستدلال تنبيها لهؤلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Siddiq” can mean habitually truthful or one who frequently affirms truth until famed for it; al-Razi prefers the first because truthful affirmation already presupposes truthfulness.
rows.anchor: مبالغة في كونه صادقا وهو الذي يكون عادته الصدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers may be called truthful affirmers because their affirmation of God and messengers is itself true.
rows.anchor: المؤمنون بالله ورسله صادقون في ذلك التصديق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophet must be truthful in every report because God confirms him; otherwise divine speech would be false, and God’s witnesses must be truthful to be accepted.
rows.anchor: النبي يجب أن يكون صادقا في كل ما أخبر عنه لأن الله تعالى صدقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though Abraham said the great idol acted and that he was sick, al-Razi says he has already demonstrated that neither statement is a lie.
rows.anchor: في قوله : { بل فعله كبيرهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every prophet is truthful, but not every truthful person is a prophet; this closeness explains why Abraham is called siddiq before nabi.
rows.anchor: ولا يجب في كل صديق أن يكون نبيا ظهر بهذا قرب مرتبة الصديق من مرتبة النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophet means one elevated in rank before God and people, especially as a mediator between God and His servants.
rows.anchor: وأما النبي فمعناه كونه رفيع القدر عند الله وعند الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Was a siddiq” may mean he became one, or that he was truthful and chaste from first existence to the end.
rows.anchor: قيل : إنه صار وقيل إن معناه وجد صديقا نبيا

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf says the clause “he was a truthful prophet” interrupts the apposition before “when he said”; alternatively, “when” attaches to “was” or to his qualities.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : هذه الجملة وقعت اعتراضا بين المبدل منه وبدله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “O my father,” the tāʾ substitutes for the possessive yāʾ; “O my father” with both would combine substitute and original, though an alif form also occurs.
rows.anchor: التاء عوض عن ياء الإضافة ولا يقال يا أبتي لئلا يجمع بين العوض والمعوض عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s first argument is that idols lack three attributes that disqualify them from divinity; worship is ultimate reverence and belongs only to the giver of every blessing.
rows.anchor: العبادة غاية التعظيم فلا يستحقها إلا من له غاية الانعام وهو الإله الذي منه أصول النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An idol that cannot hear, see, or distinguish obedience from disobedience cannot be divine; a true God must know all things.
rows.anchor: إذا لم تسمع ولم تبصر ولم تميز من يطيعها عمن يعصيها فأي فائدة في عبادتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is the core of worship, so an idol that cannot hear petitions or see an approach yields no benefit from worship or ritual proximity.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : أن الدعاء مخ العبادة فالوثن إذا لم يسمع دعاء الداعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hearing, seeing, harming, and benefiting human is better than an idol lacking these traits, so it is unfit for the better to worship the inferior.
rows.anchor: السامع المبصر الضار النافع أفضل ممن كان عاريا عن كل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If idols can neither harm nor benefit, worship offers no hoped-for gain and avoids no danger.
rows.anchor: إذا كانت لا تنفع ولا تضر فلا يرجى منها منفعة ولا يخاف من ضررها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idols cannot even protect themselves from breaking; Abraham’s ability to smash them shows there is no reason to trust them for protection.
rows.anchor: إذا كانت لا تحفظ أنفسها عن الكسر والإفساد على ما حكى الله تعالى عن إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threefold description of idols implicitly contrasts them with God, who hears, answers prayer, sees, and fulfills needs.
rows.anchor: بل الإلهية ليست إلا لربي فإنه يسمع ويجيب دعوة الداعي ويبصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Why do you worship?” refers literally to worship of idols; the later “do not worship Satan” means obey, but that figurative use gives no reason to alter the first phrase.
rows.anchor: محمول على نفس العبادة وأما قوله في المقام الثالث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Abraham’s people did not literally worship Satan, “do not worship Satan” must mean do not obey him; that figurative reading does not justify figurative interpretation of the earlier literal worship.
rows.anchor: لا يقال ذلك بل المراد الطاعة لأنهم ما كانوا يعبدون الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection proposes that Abraham’s father viewed idols as creators, planetary images, honored human intercessors, talismans tied to rare planetary conjunctions, or another excuse.
rows.anchor: فإن قيل : إما أن يقال إن أبا إبراهيم كان يعتقد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the father thought carved wood created the universe, that is manifest madness; if he believed in planets, intercession, or talismans, the stated argument does not directly disprove those doctrines.
rows.anchor: من / أجلى العلوم الضرورية ، فالشاك فيه يكون فاقدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi answers that the father’s view sought benefit from talismans or planets, and Abraham showed no benefit in obeying idols and no harm in neglecting them.
rows.anchor: على سبيل الخاصية الحاصلة من الطلسمات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says that only a complete, infallible prophet or imam can guide someone to grasp the proofs, so Abraham’s invitation seems to concede the need for such a guide.
rows.anchor: لا أنكر أنه لا بد من الدلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response denies that a prophet is necessary to understand proofs: Abraham offered the easier path, and “follow me” is advice rather than a binding command, so the alleged circularity fails.
rows.anchor: أنا ما سلمت أنه لا بد في الوقوف على الدلائل من هداية النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Do not worship Satan” means do not obey him; Abraham invokes Satan’s rebellion against God as a repellent reason to reject his counsel.
rows.anchor: لا تطعه لأنه عاص لله فنفره بهذه الصفة عن القبول منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s sincerity is shown by mentioning only Satan’s disobedience, not his enmity toward Adam; the enormity of rebellion against God filled his thought.
rows.anchor: لإمعانه في الإخلاص لم يذكر من جنايات الشيطان إلا كونه عاصيا لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disobedience to God signals poor judgment, so one should not defer to the disobedient person’s opinion.
rows.anchor: معصية الله تعالى لا تصدر إلا عن ضعيف الرأي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further objection says the argument assumes five contested claims: God exists, Satan exists, Satan rebels, no one may obey a rebel, and the father’s creed derives from Satan.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : إثبات الشيطان . وثالثها : إثبات أن الشيطان عاص لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi answers that the father may have recognized only Nimrod as deity and denied the Merciful; even if the premises were granted, the warning does not prove his belief originated with Satan.
rows.anchor: وكيف والمحكى عنه أنه ما كان يثبت إلها سوى نمروذ فكيف يسلم وجود الإله الرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenged Satan argument is a caution intended to make the father examine the earlier demonstrative proof, so the objection misses its role.
rows.anchor: فأما هذا الكلام فيجري مجرى التخويف والتحذير الذي يحمله على النظر في تلك الدلالة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra’ says “I fear” means “I know.”
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : معنى أخاف أعلم

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: Most interpreters take Abraham’s fear literally; certainty that his father would die an unbeliever is unproven, since he could still believe or persist, so fear is appropriate.
rows.anchor: والأكثرون على أنه محمول على ظاهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person is only called afraid for another when that person’s possible harm would cause pain in the one who fears, as with fear for one’s child.
rows.anchor: من يظن وصول الضرر إلى غيره فإنه لا يسمى خائفا إلا إذا كان بحيث يلزم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Satan’s ally” may mean that, after deserving punishment, the father will accompany Satan in Hell; alliance is then used figuratively for its result, although scripture says worldly friends become enemies.
rows.anchor: أنه إذا استوجب عذاب الله كان مع الشيطان في النار والولاية سبب للمعية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reading takes the punishment as God’s abandonment, after which the father becomes Satan’s ally.
rows.anchor: أن يحمل العذاب على الخذلان أي إني أخاف أن يمسك خذلان الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reading takes “ally” as one who follows after Satan, like rain that comes in succession.
rows.anchor: المطر الذي يأتي تاليا وليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satanic alliance is worse than punishment because God’s pleasure exceeds even the reward of Paradise, making its opposite worse than punishment.
rows.anchor: رضوان الله تعالى أعظم من الثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham orders his appeal carefully: disprove idols, invite reasoning over imitation, reject obedience to Satan, then warn of punishment; his repeated “O my father” shows love and concern.
rows.anchor: نبه أولا على ما يدل على المنع من عبادة الأوثان ثم أمره باتباعه في النظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s gentleness fulfills filial duty, since guiding a parent to religion is a great kindness and courtesy adds to it.
rows.anchor: قضاء لحق الأبوة على ما قال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A guide to truth must speak gently because harshness can turn a listener away and thereby become a cause of misguidance.
rows.anchor: الهادي إلى الحق لا بد وأن يكون رفيقا لطيفا يورد الكلام لا على سبيل العنف

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra says God told Abraham to cultivate good manners even with unbelievers, promising him the shelter and intimacy of the divine presence.
rows.anchor: ما روى أبو هريرة أنه قال عليه السلام : ( أوحى الله إلى إبراهيم

none: Verse text only; the segment contains the next verses without commentary.
